surprises.description: CenterPoint reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, above the preview’s $0.49–$0.50 consensus range and its $0.50–$0.51 functional whisper. That is a clear beat, though the preview had already framed the quarter as likely fine to good.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $0.49–$0.50”; “The functional whisper is $0.50–$0.51 on EPS”

surprises.description: The 2027 EPS guide is $2.07–$2.09, with a midpoint of $2.08: it meets the Street’s $2.08 consensus and reaches above the preview’s base-case range of $2.05–$2.07. This is better than the base-case framing, although it is not above consensus at the midpoint.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 EPS | $2.08”; “2027 guided $2.05–$2.07” in the base scenario

surprises.description: The 10-year capital plan rose to $70.7 billion, above the preview’s $68–$70 billion base case and its $70 billion-plus bull-case threshold. CenterPoint also said it accelerated $1.5 billion of investment into the first five years, supporting enterprise rate-base CAGR above 14% through 2030.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 10-year capital plan was increased by $4 billion to $70.7 billion, with an additional $1.5 billion of investment accelerated into the first five years, driving enterprise rate base CAGR of more than 14% through 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “plan rolled to $68–70B” in the base scenario; “plan rolled to $70B+” in the bull scenario

surprises.description: CenterPoint raised equity financing guidance by $1.6 billion to $4.5 billion, rather than delivering the preview’s most bullish outcome of a larger capital plan without additional equity. The preview explicitly identified new equity as a downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equity financing guidance was raised by a modest $1.6 billion to $4.5 billion, funding only about 25% of the $5.7 billion of total 2026 capital plan increases, well below the 47% rule of thumb.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A roll-forward to $70B+ with no new equity is the most bullish outcome available”; “Repetition of ‘no additional equity needed’ … is worth more than a 2-cent EPS beat.”

surprises.description: The large-load demand-charge figure is far below the preview’s stated expectation: the call cited roughly $6 million per gigawatt per year, versus the preview’s roughly $6 million per gigawatt per month. The charges remain outside the plan, but the reported amount is substantially lower than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Anticipates demand charges of roughly $6 million per gigawatt per year from new large loads not yet in the plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Demand charges run roughly $6M per GW per month and — critically — are not yet in the financial forecast.”

surprises.description: The preview expected about 4 GW of studied load in the Batch Zero pipeline; CenterPoint now expects only about 2 GW to stay as studied load. It still targets energizing at least 14 GW by the end of 2030, but the studied-load component is smaller than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remains confident in 10 GW of baseload, expects ~2 GW to stay as studied load, and targets energizing at least 14 GW by end of 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~14 GW expected eligible (~10 GW base load …, ~4 GW studied load…)”

surprises.description: CenterPoint raised its 2026 EPS range by one cent at both ends, rather than merely reaffirming the existing $1.89–$1.91 range. The preview expected the company to reaffirm the range or potentially signal its upper half, so this is a modest upward revision.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance range to $1.90-$1.92 from $1.89-$1.91.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 EPS | $1.91 (co. guide $1.89–$1.91, ‘at least midpoint’)”; base scenario: “FY26 reaffirmed at ‘at least midpoint’”

surprises.description: Management extended its mid-to-high-end 7%–9% EPS-growth outlook through 2030, while the preview described the existing growth framework as running through 2028. The extension gives investors a longer-dated growth commitment than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Extended expectations to grow at the mid-to-high end of its 7%-9% range through 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has guided to the ‘mid-to-high end of 7–9% annual growth through 2028.’”

surprises.description: The call identified a year-end Indiana large-load customer deal using roughly 700 MW of freed capacity, scalable to 1.4 GW. The preview noted Indiana large-load deals and a distribution-level pipeline, but did not anticipate this specific customer deal or capacity detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects a large-load Indiana customer deal by year-end, leveraging ~700 MW of freed capacity scalable to 1.4 GW.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At least $10B of upside capex” was expected to be driven in part by “Indiana large-load deals”; the preview also cited a “+2 GW distribution-level pipeline.”

surprises.description: A CAMT refund is expected to add about 60 basis points to adjusted FFO-to-debt, a credit-metric benefit the preview did not identify. The Ohio sale’s roughly 50-basis-point contribution was already anticipated, so the unexpected element is the refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ~$1.4 billion Ohio gas LDC sale (~50 bps) and a CAMT refund (~60 bps) expected to push metrics toward the higher end” of the cushion above downgrade thresholds.
